plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay only the second-highest bid, not your own. Bidding above value risks overpaying (winning at a price above value), while bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. Since this is a one-shot second-price auction with no repeated interaction to exploit, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $28, so I will bid exactly that.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, there's no incentive to bid above or below my true value of $31. Bidding higher risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me if I'm the second-highest bidder's price exceeds my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). With independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value—bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win, and bidding lower only reduces my chance of winning profitable opportunities. Since my value is $2, I will bid $2 to ensure I only win when profitable and pay a fair price if I do.
